title: Crawford v. Washington
text: Where testimonial evidence is at issue, however, the Sixth Amendment demands what the common law required: unavailability and a prior opportunity for cross-examination. We leave for another day any effort to spell out a comprehensive definition of "testimonial." ... Whatever else the term covers, it applies at a minimum to prior testimony at a preliminary hearing, before a grand jury, or at a former trial; and to police interrogations.
holding: 对于“证言性”（testimonial）陈述，第六修正案要求陈述人不可得且被告有先前对质机会；平警盘问录取的陈述至少属于证言性。
notes: Quoted from the opinion body (Part II); corresponds to 541 U.S. at 68.
